# Indiana dig-damage enforcement desk (no-code edition)

You answer actuarial questions about Indiana's dig-damage enforcement record: the Indiana Utility Regulatory
Commission's orders approving the Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee's recommendations under IC 8-1-26.
The data is 9,958 recommendation forms ("cases") from 58 orders dated 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-31.

## What you can and cannot do

You have Read, Grep and Glob only. You cannot run code, open the raw case table (it is not in this folder), or use a calculator
beyond your own arithmetic. So you answer from **pre-computed tables** in `reference/tables/`. Those tables hold counts, dollar sums,
means, medians, percentiles, histograms, name counts and top-N lists, cut by order year, base section, qualifier, respondent type and
outcome. You may combine table rows by hand: add counts and sums, take differences, ratios and shares. You may NOT invent a cut
that no table supports. When a question needs one, say so plainly and give the closest figure, labelled (see `rules.md`, section 4).

## Read order

| Step | Read | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | this README | orientation |
| 2 | `rules.md` | how to answer, the traps, how to combine rows |
| 3 | `examples.md` | the answer shape, worked from real table rows |
| 4 | `reference/tables/INDEX.md` | which table answers which kind of question, and the legend of codes |
| 5 | the one or two tables you need | Grep a table id, for example `Grep "### S7" -A 40`, rather than reading a whole file |
| 6 | `identity.md` only if unsure the question is in scope; `reference/glossary.md` for what a section or qualifier means; `reference/SCHEMA.md` for a column or known defect (Grep it, do not read it whole) |

## What is where

    README.md  identity.md  rules.md  examples.md
    reference/tables/INDEX.md          start here for numbers
    reference/tables/01_overview_time.md    totals, years, orders, quarters, damage years, lags
    reference/tables/02_cube.md             year x base section x qualifier x respondent type: counts, dollars, outcome mix
    reference/tables/03_penalty_stats.md    mean, median, percentiles, outcome mix, recommendation wording
    reference/tables/04_histograms.md       counts at each dollar value for many segments
    reference/tables/05_respondents_repeat.md   repeat names, rank, concentration, named lists
    reference/tables/06_utility_types_otherparty.md   utility companies, respondent kinds, other party
    reference/tables/07_places_committee_notes.md     cities, abstentions, notes, scan pages
    reference/glossary.md              what the sections and qualifiers mean, with an evidence tag on each statement
    reference/SCHEMA.md                the data dictionary and known defects

## If a question asks about X, go to Y

| The question asks about | Go to |
|---|---|
| a count, share or trend by order year, section, qualifier, utility or not | cube (02) or tables A, B, C (01) |
| mean, median, spread, total of penalties | 03 (S tables); the cube for sums |
| how many cases at or above $X; a percentile for an unusual cut | 04 histograms |
| repeat offenders, "the same respondent again", concentration | 05 |
| a utility company by name (CenterPoint, NIPSCO ...) | 06 U tables, and 05 T6 |
| what a section or qualifier is | `reference/glossary.md` |
| company size, digs or tickets, exposure, who excavated, fines paid, claim cost | not in the data: say so (`rules.md`, section 6) |

The question's own definitions always win over this folder. If a question defines a term differently from the preamble or from
`rules.md`, follow the question and say so in one line. If the question's definition cannot be met from the tables, say which
table gets closest.

1	# Table index: which table answers which question
2	
3	Seven files, all generated from the cleaned case table by one script. Every table is Markdown; use Grep on a table id
4	(for example `Grep "### S7"`) to jump to it, then Read a window of the file. Do not read a whole file unless you need it
5	(`05` and `03` are the biggest).
6	
7	## Legend used in every table
8	
9	- **case** = one row = one recommendation form (PREAMBLE). **year** = ORDER year (the order date's year). A table says
10	  "damage year" when it is not.
11	- **base**: base section after the PREAMBLE rule (`16(h)`, `16(i)`, `18(h)`, `18(j)`, `19(c)`, `20(a)(1)`, `20(a)(2)`,
12	  `20(a)(3)(a)`, `20(a)(3)(b)`, and `(blank)` for the one row with no cite). **qual**: the qualifier word (`expire`, `prior`, `out`,
13	  `other`, `locator-error`, `records`, `no-response`); `-` means no qualifier. **cite** = base plus qualifier, for example `16(h)(expire)`.
14	- **resp**: `U` = utility respondent (PREAMBLE prefix list), `N` = non-utility respondent (everything else).
15	- **hl** = headline penalty in dollars (first `$` amount, doubled `$` and a space after a thousands comma tolerated; no `$` = 0).
16	  **pos** = cases with hl > 0; **zero** = cases with hl = 0; **sum** (or sum_hl) = total hl in dollars; **mean** = sum / n.
17	- **Outcome class** of the recommendation text (my grouping, from the wording): **W** warning letter (any "Special instructions");
18	  **TR5** "Training, or $5,000 if the respondent fails to train" (hl = 5000 although training avoids it); **TO** training only
19	  (hl 0); **PT** a dollar penalty the respondent may mitigate or replace by training (for example "$1,500, respondent can complete
20	  training instead of paying $1,500"); **F** a flat dollar penalty with no training wording; **X** none of those (no `$`, no
21	  warning, no training: 'Other', blank, a bare number). W, TR5, TO, PT, F, X add up to n.
22	- Percentiles are nearest-rank; the median of an even n is the average of the two middle values.
23	- Medians, percentiles and distinct-name counts CANNOT be added across rows. Counts, sums and histogram columns can.
24	
25	## By kind of question
26	
27	| Question is about | Table(s) | File |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| Total cases, orders, utility vs non-utility, data-quality counts, duplicates | Data-size block, A | 01 |
30	| Frequency by order year; cases per order; orders per year | A, D, D2 | 01 |
31	| Trend by quarter | E | 01 |
32	| Cases by base section and year (all, U only, N only) | B, B-U, B-N | 01 |
33	| Which section letters exist when (16(h) vs 16(i), 18(h) vs 18(j)) | B3 | 01 |
34	| Qualifier counts, qualifier by year, qualifier by base section | C, C2 | 01 |
35	| Damage year, seasonality (damage month), cases by damage year x base or resp | F1-F6 | 01 |
36	| Lags: damage to order, meeting to order; committee-meeting year | G, G2, G3, G4 | 01 |
37	| **Any count / sum / outcome mix for year x base x qualifier x resp** (recombine by hand) | the cube | 02 |
38	| Severity: mean, median, quartiles, p90, max, zero share, by year, base, qualifier, cite, resp and combinations | S0-S9 | 03 |
39	| Share of warnings / training / flat penalties; $ by outcome | O1-O6 | 03 |
40	| What the recommendation text actually says; warning-letter instructions | R, R2, R3 | 03 |
41	| Number of cases at or above a dollar threshold; any percentile or median for a custom cut | histograms H0-H7 (add the columns) | 04 |
42	| Repeat offenders: how many names have k+ cases, how concentrated | T1, T1b, T1c, T9 | 05 |
43	| Names present in several years / orders | T2, T2b | 05 |
44	| Effect of merging name spellings | T3, T3b | 05 |
45	| Does the 2nd / 3rd case of a name get a different penalty; share of cases that are repeats | T4, T4b, T4c | 05 |
46	| Time between repeat damages | T4d | 05 |
47	| Named lists: non-utility names with 4+ cases (T5), every utility name (T6), top by $ (T7), top names per year (T8, and non-utility only T8N), per section (T10) | T5-T8, T8N, T10 | 05 |
48	| Utility respondents by company: cases, years, sections, outcomes, severity | U1-U5 | 06 |
49	| Kinds of respondent (government, telecom, energy/water, contractor, other) by keyword | N-N5 | 06 |
50	| The other party (who was on the other side; utility other party) | P-P4 | 06 |
51	| Cities and places | L, L2, L3 | 07 |
52	| Abstentions, notes in additional_info, scan pages | M, M2, K, K2, K3 | 07 |
53	
54	## How to pick
55	
56	1. Count or total on year / section / qualifier / resp: sum cells of the cube (02), or read 01.
57	2. Mean = sum / n from the cube or from a stats table. Median, quartile or "share above $X": stats tables (03) when the cut is listed
58	   there; otherwise a histogram (04): walk the cumulative counts.
59	3. Names: file 05 (exact names). A "top" list is complete down to the stated cut; below it, say you cannot list them.
60	4. If no table has the cut, say so and give the closest labelled figure (see rules.md, section 4).

# Table index: which table answers which question

Seven files, all generated from the cleaned case table by one script. Every table is Markdown; use Grep on a table id
(for example `Grep "### S7"`) to jump to it, then Read a window of the file. Do not read a whole file unless you need it
(`05` and `03` are the biggest).

## Legend used in every table

- **case** = one row = one recommendation form (PREAMBLE). **year** = ORDER year (the order date's year). A table says
  "damage year" when it is not.
- **base**: base section after the PREAMBLE rule (`16(h)`, `16(i)`, `18(h)`, `18(j)`, `19(c)`, `20(a)(1)`, `20(a)(2)`,
  `20(a)(3)(a)`, `20(a)(3)(b)`, and `(blank)` for the one row with no cite). **qual**: the qualifier word (`expire`, `prior`, `out`,
  `other`, `locator-error`, `records`, `no-response`); `-` means no qualifier. **cite** = base plus qualifier, for example `16(h)(expire)`.
- **resp**: `U` = utility respondent (PREAMBLE prefix list), `N` = non-utility respondent (everything else).
- **hl** = headline penalty in dollars (first `$` amount, doubled `$` and a space after a thousands comma tolerated; no `$` = 0).
  **pos** = cases with hl > 0; **zero** = cases with hl = 0; **sum** (or sum_hl) = total hl in dollars; **mean** = sum / n.
- **Outcome class** of the recommendation text (my grouping, from the wording): **W** warning letter (any "Special instructions");
  **TR5** "Training, or $5,000 if the respondent fails to train" (hl = 5000 although training avoids it); **TO** training only
  (hl 0); **PT** a dollar penalty the respondent may mitigate or replace by training (for example "$1,500, respondent can complete
  training instead of paying $1,500"); **F** a flat dollar penalty with no training wording; **X** none of those (no `$`, no
  warning, no training: 'Other', blank, a bare number). W, TR5, TO, PT, F, X add up to n.
- Percentiles are nearest-rank; the median of an even n is the average of the two middle values.
- Medians, percentiles and distinct-name counts CANNOT be added across rows. Counts, sums and histogram columns can.

## By kind of question

| Question is about | Table(s) | File |
|---|---|---|
| Total cases, orders, utility vs non-utility, data-quality counts, duplicates | Data-size block, A | 01 |
| Frequency by order year; cases per order; orders per year | A, D, D2 | 01 |
| Trend by quarter | E | 01 |
| Cases by base section and year (all, U only, N only) | B, B-U, B-N | 01 |
| Which section letters exist when (16(h) vs 16(i), 18(h) vs 18(j)) | B3 | 01 |
| Qualifier counts, qualifier by year, qualifier by base section | C, C2 | 01 |
| Damage year, seasonality (damage month), cases by damage year x base or resp | F1-F6 | 01 |
| Lags: damage to order, meeting to order; committee-meeting year | G, G2, G3, G4 | 01 |
| **Any count / sum / outcome mix for year x base x qualifier x resp** (recombine by hand) | the cube | 02 |
| Severity: mean, median, quartiles, p90, max, zero share, by year, base, qualifier, cite, resp and combinations | S0-S9 | 03 |
| Share of warnings / training / flat penalties; $ by outcome | O1-O6 | 03 |
| What the recommendation text actually says; warning-letter instructions | R, R2, R3 | 03 |
| Number of cases at or above a dollar threshold; any percentile or median for a custom cut | histograms H0-H7 (add the columns) | 04 |
| Repeat offenders: how many names have k+ cases, how concentrated | T1, T1b, T1c, T9 | 05 |
| Names present in several years / orders | T2, T2b | 05 |
| Effect of merging name spellings | T3, T3b | 05 |
| Does the 2nd / 3rd case of a name get a different penalty; share of cases that are repeats | T4, T4b, T4c | 05 |
| Time between repeat damages | T4d | 05 |
| Named lists: non-utility names with 4+ cases (T5), every utility name (T6), top by $ (T7), top names per year (T8, and non-utility only T8N), per section (T10) | T5-T8, T8N, T10 | 05 |
| Utility respondents by company: cases, years, sections, outcomes, severity | U1-U5 | 06 |
| Kinds of respondent (government, telecom, energy/water, contractor, other) by keyword | N-N5 | 06 |
| The other party (who was on the other side; utility other party) | P-P4 | 06 |
| Cities and places | L, L2, L3 | 07 |
| Abstentions, notes in additional_info, scan pages | M, M2, K, K2, K3 | 07 |

## How to pick

1. Count or total on year / section / qualifier / resp: sum cells of the cube (02), or read 01.
2. Mean = sum / n from the cube or from a stats table. Median, quartile or "share above $X": stats tables (03) when the cut is listed
   there; otherwise a histogram (04): walk the cumulative counts.
3. Names: file 05 (exact names). A "top" list is complete down to the stated cut; below it, say you cannot list them.
4. If no table has the cut, say so and give the closest labelled figure (see rules.md, section 4).

**Numerator:** cases with a headline above $0 whose recommendation mentions training. Only the TR5 and PT outcome classes have both (TR5 2,361 + PT 1,186 = 3,547). Their zero counts are 0 in table 03, S9 (line 238 and line 240), so all of them have a headline above $0. The TO class (19 cases) has training wording but a headline of $0, so it is excluded.

**Denominator:** all cases with a headline above $0 = total cases − zero-headline cases = 9,958 − (2,033 W + 19 TO + 7 X) = 7,899. This matches TR5 + PT + F = 2,361 + 1,186 + 4,352 = 7,899.

**Check:** the training-mention total in table 03, R3 (3,566) equals TR5 + PT + TO (2,361 + 1,186 + 19), so the training wording is confined to those three classes.

3,547 / 7,899 = 0.44905 → **44.9%**
